adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now iterates `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` to create multiple calendar events (and `handleNewBooking` appends team members’ destination calendars for COLLECTIVE via `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`). However, when persisting the booking, the write path still only connects a single destination calendar: `connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }`, implying the Booking model remains single-valued. Many subsequent flows in this diff rebuild `evt.destinationCalendar` from `booking.destinationCalendar` by wrapping it in a one-element array (e.g., cron/payment/confirm/editLocation/reschedule handlers), so they cannot reconstruct the full set of destinations created at booking time and must rely on references for non-primary calendars. This is a real consistency/architecture concern grounded in the diff, but the diff alone doesn’t prove it causes incorrect behavior (it may be an intentional “primary destination only” persistence choice).
